Oral Order 06/ Dated: 14.03.2024:
The instant appeal filed under Section 21 (1) (4) of the National Investigation Agency
Act, 2008, is directed against the order dated
02.09.2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-I cum Special Judge Pocso,
Lohardaga in M.C.A. No. 445 of 2023/ Spl. Pocso 37/23, by which the prayer for regular bail of the
appellant in connection with Kuru P.S. Case No. 69 of 2023, registered under Sections 363/ 366
(A)/ 376 (Da)/ 370/34 of the Ipc and Section 6 of the Pocso Act, has been rejected.
2.

It is contended on behalf of the appellant that there is no allegation said to attract the ingredients of Sections 363/ 366A/ 376 (DA)/ 370/34 of the Indian Penal Code as also under Section 6 of the POCSO Act, since, against the appellant there is no allegation of either kidnapping or subject to rape of the victim, so as to attract any of the penal offences, upon which the first information report has been instituted.

It has further been contended that the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr. P.C. which has been appended with the counter affidavit, even if there is no disclosure by the victim at the time of recording her statement under Section 164 Cr.

P.C. is said to attract any of the penal offences, rather only involvement has been shown that co-accused persons, namely, Moin Ansari and Shahbaj Ansari who after committed rape have given call to the present appellant for the purpose of selling Serajul Ansari vs State Of Jharkhand on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117396686/
1 the victim.

sentences.text: But even there is no allegation against the appellant who was involved in selling of the victim, since, the victim was carried to Railway station by one Sahbaj Ansari and Moin Ansari who on foot had carried the victim to the railway station from where the victim has tried to manage to escape.
3. Learned counsel further submitted that appellant is languishing in judicial custody since 01.06.2023 as also the chargesheet has been submitted.
Further the appellant is having no criminal antecedent as per the State itself, as per para 5 of the objection petition filed by the State.
4. While on the other hand learned counsel appearing for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
It has been submitted that by referring the first information report that the appellant is also directly involved in commission of crime along with the other co-accused Moin Ansari and Sahbaj Ansari.

It has been submitted that the bail application of Sahbaj Ansari vide order dated 07.02.2024 passed in Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1916 of 2023 has already been rejected, hence the present appeal is also fit to be dismissed.

5. This Court has considered the rival submission made on behalf of the parties, impugned order,
case diary, objection petition is required to considered the imputation so made against the appellant, forensic report, first information report, material collected for investigation as recorded in the case diary and the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr. P.C. as appended no objection by the State.
It is evident from the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr. P.C. that the specific attributability has been casted upon Moin Ansari and Sahbaj Ansari who had subjected the victim for rape.
Both the accused persons, namely, Moin Ansari and Sahbaj Ansari after committing rape upon the victim, gave telephonic call to the present appellant.
Based upon which, at the place of occurrence they have planned to sale out the victim.

6. It has also come in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr. P.C. that the appellant has not carried the victim to the railway station rather Moin Ansari and Sahbaj Ansari who had carried the victim to the railway station for the purpose of selling.
However, the girl has managed to escape.

So far as the implication of the appellant so as to attract the penal offence under Section 366 IPC is concerned, this Court prima facie is of the view that at the moment there is no ingredient to attract the offence.

7. This Court therefore is of the view that so far as ground taken by the learned State counsel that one of the co-accused namely Sahbaj Ansari whose bail appeal has been rejected by a coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 07.02.2024 passed in Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1916 of 2023

,
therefore, the requirement is to consider the allegation of Sahbaj Ansari whose implication in the petition alleged against the present appellant, so as to come to the conclusion as to whether issue of parity is to apply or not.

sentences.text:
It is evident from the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr. P.C. that there is a specific allegation against Sahbaj Ansari on commission of rape and thereafter Sahbaj Ansari along with the another co-accused namely, Moin Ansari had carried the victim on foot to the railway station for the purpose of selling.
As such

, it is evident from the statement so recorded under Section 164 Cr. P.C. that the case of Sahbaj Ansari who has subjected the victim to rape is quite distinct to that of the allegation as levelled against the present appellant, since, there is no allegation to establish the physical relationship with the victim by the appellant.
The appellant is languishing in judicial custody since 01.06.2023, who is having no criminal antecedent as also the chargesheet has been submitted.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the impugned order needs to be interfered.
9. Accordingly, the impugned order is hereby quashed and set aside.
10. In view thereof, the instant appeal stands allowed.

11. In consequence thereof, the appellant, above named, is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned C.J.M, Lohardaga, in connection with Kuru P.S. Case No. 69 of 2023, subject to the condition that the appellant will cooperate in the trial and shall appear on each and every date before the learned trial court, failing which, the learned trial court is at liberty to take appropriate course in accordance with law and; further subject to the condition that one of the bailers should be close relative of the appellant, which is to be accompanied by affidavit justifying that such bailer is close relative of the appellant.
12. Any observation made by us in aforesaid paragraphs shall not be construed as commenced on the merit of the case.
13. Accordingly, the instant appeal stands disposed of.

(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Arun Kumar Rai, J.) Pramanik/
